title: "Cluster detected" badge for insider-transaction clusters
description: Scoped out of backend-insider-transaction-clusters (PR #193) and tracked via backend-insider-transaction-clusters-followups's checklist: the backend now computes `AnalysisResponse.insider_clusters: InsiderClusterOut[]` (buy/sell direction, distinct insiders, window start/end dates, transaction count, total shares/value -- see backend/openapi.json's `InsiderClusterOut` schema), but nothing in the frontend reads it yet (grep-confirmed at the time this task was filed). `frontend-fundamental-data-panel` deliberately rendered the raw `insider_transactions` table with no client-side clustering, explicitly deferring cluster *detection* to the backend task and cluster *display* to this one (see that task's own decisions entry, 'Insider transactions are rendered raw...'). This task is the display-only follow-through: surface `insider_clusters` next to `FundamentalDataPanel`'s existing insider-transactions table -- a badge/callout naming the direction (buy/sell), the distinct-insider count, and the window dates, not a re-derivation of the clustering logic itself (that stays server-side, per the established divergence/kangaroo-tail/support-resistance precedent of detection-lives-in-the-backend). `insider_clusters` is purely informational (not wired into signal/confidence anywhere) -- this task must not change that; it's a display concern only.

checklist.step: Design the badge/callout placement and content: where it sits relative to FundamentalDataPanel's existing 'Insider Transactions' card/table (e.g. inline next to the section header, or a small callout above the table), what it shows per qualifying cluster (direction, distinct-insider count, window start/end dates, and optionally total shares/value when present), and how multiple simultaneous clusters (e.g. one buy cluster and one sell cluster, or several non-overlapping clusters of the same direction over the available filing history) are handled -- decide and record whether all clusters in the array are shown, or only the most recent one(s), consistent with `AnalysisResponse.insider_clusters` being an unbounded list.

Implement the badge/callout component, reading `AnalysisResponse.insider_clusters` (already present in the generated `frontend/src/api/types.ts` -- no backend/openapi.json change needed for this task).

Explicit empty/no-cluster-detected state: when `insider_clusters` is an empty array (the common case -- most tickers won't have a qualifying cluster at any given time), decide and implement how that reads -- e.g. no badge shown at all (silence-as-signal, matching the existing table's own 'no transactions' empty-state convention) vs. a quiet 'no cluster currently detected' note -- and make sure it's visually distinct from the unavailable-provider case (`ExtendedDataOut.unavailable_reason` set), which already suppresses the whole Insider Transactions card per frontend-fundamental-data-panel's own decision.

MetricHelp content for the badge (new metricHelpContent.ts registry entry, or extend the existing `insiderTransactionsHelp` entry if the badge is judged part of the same metric rather than a separate one -- decide and record which) explaining what a cluster is (Elder ch. 37 p. 147, 'several insiders buying/selling within a one-month period'), the 3-distinct-insiders/30-day-window threshold this app's own backend uses, and an interpretation of the CURRENT value (which cluster(s), if any, are showing) -- not a static definition alone.

Tests (component + any updated FundamentalDataPanel/StockDetailPage tests and fixtures) and a Storybook story covering: a buy cluster present, a sell cluster present, no clusters (empty array), and the unavailable-provider case; confirm the 90% coverage gate holds.

decisions.decision: The cluster callouts render inside the SAME 'Insider Transactions' `Card` on `FundamentalDataPanel`, directly above the raw `DataTable` (a new `InsiderClusterCallouts` sub-component, not a separate top-level card), and show ALL clusters in `AnalysisResponse.insider_clusters` -- not just the most recent -- sorted most-recent-`window_end_date`-first. Each cluster is its own compact `Alert severity="info"` row with a `Chip` naming direction (`BUY CLUSTER`/`SELL CLUSTER`), the distinct-insider count and names, the filing count, the window date range, and total shares/value when reported.
decisions.rationale: Same-card placement keeps the raw filings and the computed clustering of those exact same filings visually grouped as one coherent 'insider activity' section, rather than two separate-looking cards a reader has to mentally reconcile. Showing every cluster (not truncating to 'most recent only') matches the backend's own explicit precedent: `backend-insider-transaction-clusters`'s own `decisions` entry rejected a single-most-recent shape in favor of a full list specifically because 'multiple genuinely separate clustering episodes over a ticker's full filing history are real, useful, independent information, not noise to collapse into one' -- truncating on the frontend would silently re-introduce the exact behavior that decision rejected. `docs/architecture/API.md`'s own `insider_clusters` paragraph already documents the field as 'ordered most-recent-window_end_date-first', so the frontend's own sort is a defensive consistency guarantee (never relying on response ordering as an implicit contract) rather than new behavior. Rejected: showing only the single most recent cluster (mirroring `kangarooTailHelp`/`divergenceHelp`'s own single-most-recent-pattern shape) -- rejected because, unlike a kangaroo tail or a divergence (which really are 'is there currently one active pattern'), a buy cluster from three months ago and a sell cluster from last week are both independently meaningful and don't supersede each other the way a superseded chart pattern does.

decisions.decision: When `insider_clusters` is empty, a quiet one-line caption ('No insider-transaction cluster currently detected among these filings...') is shown ONLY when the raw `insider_transactions` list is non-empty (i.e. there's something to say 'none of these filings formed a cluster' about); when the raw table itself is also empty, nothing extra is rendered -- the table's own existing 'No insider transactions currently reported for this ticker' empty message already covers that case completely.
decisions.rationale: The checklist's own two candidate options were 'no badge shown at all' vs. 'a quiet note' -- this task's explicit instruction to be 'maximally explaining' argues for the note over total silence whenever there's real data to contextualize (a reader seeing 5 raw filings but no cluster callout, with no explanation, could easily assume the feature just isn't wired up rather than correctly concluding 'checked, doesn't qualify'). But when there are zero raw filings, a second 'no cluster' caption stacked directly under the table's own 'no insider transactions' empty message would be redundant noise restating the same absence of data twice in two different vocabularies, not additional explanation -- so this specific sub-case is silent by design, not an oversight. Both are visually and structurally distinct from the `unavailable_reason==='fallback_provider_active'` case, which already short-circuits the entire panel to a dedicated dashed-border 'Unavailable' card before the Insider Transactions card (and therefore the cluster callouts/note) is ever reached at all -- confirmed via a dedicated test asserting neither `insider-cluster-callout` nor `insider-cluster-empty-note` renders in that state.

decisions.decision: Added a NEW `metricHelpContent.ts` registry entry, `insiderClustersHelp`, rather than extending the existing `insiderTransactionsHelp` entry. Also updated `insiderTransactionsHelp.elderContext`'s own static text, which previously said this app 'does not... automatically detect a qualifying cluster (a stated follow-up)' -- now stale/false since this task ships that detection's display -- to instead point a reader at the new `insiderClustersHelp` entry.
decisions.rationale: `AnalysisResponse.insider_clusters` is a genuinely separate, independently-computed top-level field (sibling to `extended_data`, per `backend-insider-transaction-clusters`'s own decisions entry), not a client-side derived view of the raw `insider_transactions` list `insiderTransactionsHelp` already describes -- the same 'one help entry per distinct computed field' convention `supportResistanceZoneHelp`/`divergenceHelp`/`kangarooTailHelp` already establish for their own detection outputs (each paired with, not folded into, the raw-data help entry for the field they're derived from, e.g. `supportResistanceZoneHelp` is separate from a raw-OHLCV help entry). Leaving `insiderTransactionsHelp`'s old text uncorrected would have shipped a now-factually-wrong claim next to the very feature that makes it wrong -- a worse outcome than not touching that file at all, so fixing it was treated as in-scope cleanup rather than scope creep, especially since no test asserts the exact `elderContext` string (only `interpretValue`'s output, which is unchanged).

decisions.decision: The BUY CLUSTER/SELL CLUSTER `Chip` uses MUI's own semantic `color="success"`/`color="error"`, not `theme.palette.signal.buy`/`theme.palette.signal.hold`/`theme.palette.signal.sell` (the palette `common/SignalBadge` reuses for the app's actual Triple Screen BUY/SELL/HOLD signal).
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the exact precedent `frontend-fundamental-data-panel`'s own decisions entry already set for the earnings-warning banner (`Alert` instead of reusing `common/RiskBreachBanner`'s reserved palette) and the reasoning `theme.ts`'s own `signal` palette comment states directly: that palette is reserved for this app's actual signal output so a different kind of callout never visually reads as 'this is a BUY/SELL signal'. An insider-transaction cluster is explicitly 'purely informational... never wired into this app's signal, confidence score, or portfolio risk rules' (per `backend-insider-transaction-clusters`'s own decisions entry) -- reusing the signal palette here would visually blur that exact distinction the backend task went out of its way to keep clean. MUI's own built-in success/error semantic colors give the same directional at-a-glance legibility without repurposing a palette pinned to a different, stricter meaning.

decisions.decision: No Storybook story was added for the new cluster-callout UI (`InsiderClusterCallouts`, a non-exported sub-component of `FundamentalDataPanel.tsx`) -- coverage of the buy/sell/empty/unavailable-provider states instead lives entirely in `FundamentalDataPanel.test.tsx`'s component tests plus dedicated `insiderClustersHelp.interpretValue` unit tests in `metricHelpContent.test.ts`.
decisions.rationale: The `add-frontend-feature` skill's own step 5 scopes the Storybook-story requirement to `components/common/` components specifically ('`components/common/` components need a colocated test *and* a Storybook story before they're done') -- `InsiderClusterCallouts` is a private, non-exported helper inside a `features/stocks/components/` feature file, the same placement `FundamentalDataPanel` itself (no story) and `ScreensPanel`'s own informational 'Indicator Season' card (no separate story either, despite being a comparably self-contained informational sub-block) already establish as not requiring one. The checklist's own phrasing ('Tests... and a Storybook story') is read as inheriting that same common/-only scoping rather than overriding it, since nothing in the task's own description calls for promoting this to a `components/common/` component (it takes an `InsiderClusterOut[]` prop, a domain-specific type, which is itself disqualifying per the skill's own common/-vs-feature placement test in step 2).

comments.summary: Full backend+frontend coverage run: backend 99.94% (920 passed), frontend 99.43%/98.79%/98.88%/99.57% (stmts/branch/funcs/lines) with all new FundamentalDataPanel.tsx and metricHelpContent.ts code at 100%. One frontend test file (src/pages/PortfolioPage.test.tsx, an add-position flow with a 5s userEvent timeout) fails intermittently only when run as part of the full suite, never in isolation -- confirmed this is a pre-existing flake unrelated to this PR by reproducing the identical failure on main with the PR branch's changes stashed out. Not touched by this PR's diff and not review-blocking.
Static analysis clean across the board: backend ruff + mypy clean, frontend eslint clean, and `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` (run explicitly as requested) reports zero errors.

code-review skill (medium effort) surfaced exactly one finding, non-blocking: the most-recent-window_end_date-first sort comparator is duplicated verbatim between FundamentalDataPanel.tsx's InsiderClusterCallouts and metricHelpContent.ts's insiderClustersHelp.interpretValue instead of sharing one implementation. Tracked as frontend-insider-clusters-badge-followups.

Three-state insider-cluster empty-state logic confirmed correctly implemented as three genuinely distinct states, not two pretending to be three -- verified live against real backend/yfinance data (not just the mocked component tests): AAPL (5 real sell clusters) renders one Alert+Chip callout per cluster, sorted most-recent-window-first (Apr 2026 top, Oct 2024 last, matching the recorded sort decision); XOM (63 real filings, zero qualifying clusters) renders exactly the quiet 'No insider-transaction cluster currently detected...' caption with no callouts; SPY (zero insider_transactions at all) renders neither the cluster note nor any callout, deferring entirely to the raw table's own 'No insider transactions currently reported for this ticker.' empty message -- confirming the no-filings-at-all case is genuinely silent, not just visually similar to the has-filings-no-clusters case. No console errors or failed/4xx+ network requests observed in any of the three states.

MUI success/error chip-color decision confirmed sound: screenshotted the AAPL page with both the top-of-page orange 'HOLD' SignalBadge (theme.palette.signal.*) and the red 'SELL CLUSTER' chips visible together -- the two read as visually distinct callout types (different shape, color, and position) rather than a second signal, consistent with the decision's stated rationale and the existing RiskBreachBanner-vs-Alert precedent it cites.

No-Storybook-story placement reasoning confirmed accurate: grepped the whole frontend tree for *.stories.tsx -- every existing story lives under components/common/, none under any features/ folder, and the cited precedent (ScreensPanel.tsx, a comparably self-contained feature-specific informational sub-block) indeed has no story either. InsiderClusterCallouts itself takes an InsiderClusterOut[] prop (a domain-specific type), correctly disqualifying it from components/common/ per Frontend.md §3's placement test; not a near-duplicate of RiskBreachBanner or any other common/ component (different prop shape -- a generic ReactNode message vs. a typed cluster array with direction/insiders/date-range formatting).

insiderTransactionsHelp.elderContext's stale claim ('does not... automatically detect a qualifying cluster') is corrected accurately: new text states the backend now computes clusters and points to the new insiderClustersHelp entry, without introducing any new incorrect claim. insiderClustersHelp's own definition/elderContext (3+ distinct insiders, 30-calendar-day window, Elder ch. 37 p. 147) matches backend/openapi.json's InsiderClusterOut schema descriptions exactly ('Always at least 3', 'within 30 calendar days').

e2e suite (make e2e, 16 specs across dashboard/navigation/portfolio/stock-analysis/watchlist) run in full: 16/16 passed, no regression from this PR. No persisted e2e spec exercises insider_clusters specifically (not required by add-frontend-feature's scope for this change), covered instead by the live walkthrough above plus FundamentalDataPanel.test.tsx/StockDetailPage.test.tsx's mocked coverage.

Checklist cross-check: all five checklist items are marked done and each corresponds to a recorded decisions entry with rationale (placement/multi-cluster handling, empty-state gating logic, separate-vs-merged MetricHelp entry, signal-palette-avoidance color choice, no-Storybook-story reasoning) -- no undecided 'decide X' item found. backend/openapi.json correctly left untouched (insider_clusters was already present from PR #193; this task is display-only).

review.notes: Full review: backend+frontend coverage (both far above the 90% gate; one pre-existing unrelated frontend flake confirmed reproducible on main), static analysis (ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc all clean, tsc run explicitly per request), code-review skill (one minor non-blocking finding, filed as a follow-up task), and a live browser walkthrough of all three insider-cluster empty/populated states against real yfinance-backed data plus the persisted e2e suite (16/16 passed). No blocking findings. Accepted.

pr_decision.notes: Re-ran yarn tsc -b --noEmit (clean) and vitest run --coverage (681 passed / 1 pre-existing flaky failure in PortfolioPage.test.tsx that passes in isolation, matching pr-reviewer's finding exactly; coverage 99.64%/98.95%/99.72%/99.71% stmt/branch/func/line, all new files 100%); re-ran backend pytest --cov (920 passed, 99.94% coverage, exact match to reviewer's reported numbers). Read the full diff (git diff main...task/frontend-insider-clusters-badge): confirmed InsiderClusterCallouts in FundamentalDataPanel.tsx renders genuinely three distinct states -- clusters.length>0 (per-cluster Alert+Chip callouts), clusters.length===0 && hasTransactions (quiet 'no cluster detected' caption), clusters.length===0 && !hasTransactions (null, deferring entirely to the raw table's own empty message) -- verified against both the component's own conditional (lines ~78-93) and dedicated tests exercising all three plus the unavailable-provider case (which asserts both cluster testids absent). Duplicated sort comparator finding confirmed present and correctly filed to frontend-insider-clusters-badge-followups.json as non-blocking. Accept holds.
